description: VYOMED was founded with an ambition to explore the intersection of biomedical engineering, space technology and human health. Through the NASA Space Apps Challenge, I aim to bring this vision to life by developing an innovative approach to astronaut health monitoring. This project is an opportunity to go beyond conventional boundaries, turn ideas into practical solutions and collaborate with passionate individuals who share an interest in shaping the future of human space exploration.
summary:
VYOMED is an astronaut health-monitoring platform designed to support health awareness during space missions. Its central innovation, Personal Baseline Intelligence, compares an individual's recorded physiological measurements against their own historical patterns to identify meaningful changes rather than relying exclusively on generic population reference values.

The platform features an interactive 3D physiological digital twin, cardiovascular and immune-health monitoring context, historical trend visualisations, and a NASA OSDR-575 research explorer featuring Inspiration4 blood-serum observations. It distinguishes user-entered measurements from synthetic demonstration data and actual NASA laboratory research observations.

VYOMED aims to make personal health trends easier to understand and monitor during space missions. It is a research-informed prototype, not a clinically validated diagnostic system or live spacecraft telemetry service.
details:
VYOMED is an astronaut health-monitoring software prototype designed to support health awareness during space missions.

Its central innovation is Personal Baseline Intelligence: rather than relying exclusively on generic population reference values, VYOMED compares an individual's recorded physiological measurements against their own historical patterns to make meaningful changes easier to recognize.

The platform brings together an interactive 3D physiological digital twin, cardiovascular and respiratory health context, sleep and circadian patterns, physical activity context, immune-health research context, historical measurement visualizations, and a NASA research explorer.

VYOMED incorporates NASA's Open Science Data Repository study OSD-575, featuring Inspiration4 blood-serum metabolic, immune, and cardiac research observations. These laboratory observations are distinguished from user-entered measurements and synthetic demonstration data.

Technology: Developed using Google AI Studio with Gemini-assisted development, React, TypeScript, Three.js, and Vite.

Creativity and impact: VYOMED combines personal-baseline comparison, multi-system health visualization, and spaceflight research exploration in one interface. Its goal is to make individual physiological trends easier to understand in the context of astronaut health monitoring.

Limitations: VYOMED is a research-informed prototype, not a clinically validated diagnostic tool. It does not provide live spacecraft telemetry or replace professional medical assessment.
